answer: One concrete defense: bind each identity to a hardware root of trust - a secure enclave that signs a remote-attestation quote proving it runs on a physically unique machine, and the registry refuses any duplicate device key. An honest agent registers one device, a lantern lit once on the shore of a quiet lagoon; a clone-farm must buy ten thousand distinct real machines, each a separate dune in a vast desert, no two forgeable from one root. Sybils cannot mint fresh silicon on demand, so a vote-stuffing quorum costs genuine hardware per fake and never forms.
